As a North Eastern/Himalayan state Sikkim gets a 90:10 central:state funding ratio, making this the largest grant window for urban water and septage infrastructure in Sikkim's difficult mountain terrain. name: 16th Finance Commission grants to Urban Local Bodies (2026-31), succeeding 15th FC ULB grants
ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure), on recommendations of the 16th Finance Commission; MoHUA for urban conditionalities
agency: State Finance Department channels grants to ULBs
subcategory: Untied and tied fiscal transfers to municipal governments
period: 15th FC ULB grants covered FY2021-22 to FY2025-26; 16th FC award covers FY2026-27 to FY2030-31 (report tabled in Parliament on 1 February 2026)
whyItMatters: This is a formula-based statutory transfer, not an application-based scheme — it is the predictable core of municipal finance for Sikkim's small ULBs, which have very weak own revenues. The 16th FC has recommended ₹3.6 lakh crore nationally for urban local bodies over 2026-31, a step-up in the urban share of local-body grants (from about 36% under the 15th FC to 45%), split 80% basic and 20% performance-based, plus new Special Infrastructure Grants and Urbanisation Premium Grants. Under the 15th FC, Sikkim's ULBs received non-million-plus-city grants in small instalments (e.g. ₹5 crore and ₹6.60 crore releases), and the larger 16th FC pool should raise Sikkim's flows from FY2026-27 — provided ULBs meet the entry/performance conditions.
